pages.title: Rules
pages.text: $(li)$(bold)PvP is on$() and there are $(bold)no land claims$(). Pick your spot with care, keep valuables close, and settle things like adults.$(br)$(li)$(bold)Die and your items wait in a grave$() where you fell. Only you can open it (a teammate can with your permission).$(br)$(li)$(bold)Waystones, but no teleport commands.$() Waystones stand in villages, on towers and at shrines. Activate one and you can warp back to it later, and you can take found ones home. See $(l:lemursaucepacket:waystones)Waystones$(/l). Everyday travel is by train, airship, horse and happy ghast, so the rail network still matters. Nether
portals are linked properly (a portal always leads back where it came from).$(br)$(li)$(bold)The launcher decides the mods.$() Your own extras go in its Mods tab.

pages.title: Lemurton, the spawn city
pages.text: A new world starts you in $(bold)Lemurton$(), a walled town in the style of RuneScape's Varrock and Lumbridge, built by the server the first time it starts. It has:$(br2)$(li)a plaza with a fountain and the $(bold)Lemurton waystone$(), visible to everyone from the start;$(br)$(li)a market of stalls;$(br)$(li)shops and townhouses on the ring streets, and cottages by the walls;$(br)$(li)four gates.$(br2)Lemurton is a $(bold)safe zone$():

$(li)Nobody can break or place blocks there, pour lava or water, or start fires.$(br)$(li)Players can't hurt each other, and hostile mobs don't spawn (any that wander in are removed).$(br)$(li)Doors, chests, waystones, shops and the townsfolk all work as usual.$(br2)Admins build there in creative mode. A world that existed before the city came to the pack doesn't get one.

pages.title: What's different from vanilla
pages.text: $(li)$(bold)Create is the spine.$() Every stage of progress runs through Create machines; other mods feed it (ore veins, crops, coins) or give it a reason to exist (structures, an economy, airships).$(br)$(li)$(bold)Terrain:$() Terralith, Regions Unexplored and Nullscape rework the Overworld and the End, with new trees and woods.$(br)$(li)$(bold)Structures:$() When Dungeons Arise, YUNG's structures, Create-themed ruins and towns, and tall towers with a waystone on top. Loot chests are per player (Lootr), so nobody gets beaten to one.$(br)$(li)$(bold)Ore veins:$() Create Ore Excavation adds infinite veins you find

with a prospector and drill with Create machines.$(br)$(li)$(bold)Economy:$() Numismatics coins pay for quests and missions and buy from other players' vendors.$(br)$(li)$(bold)Skills:$() RuneScape-style levels gate weapons, tools and armour and make you stronger. See $(l:lemursaucepacket:skills)Skills$(/l).$(br)$(li)$(bold)Hard blocks need Hardness:$() a pickaxe tier alone doesn't break the good stuff. Iron needs a Hardness I tome on your pickaxe (crafted from andesite, copper and a book), gold and redstone Hardness II (or a Mechanical Drill on a contraption, which breaks up to tier II), diamonds and obsidian H

ardness III, ancient debris IV, with Mining levels to match. Found some before you can mine it? You can keep it in a chest or drop it, but recipes, machines and other containers refuse it until your Mining level is there. Early obsidian for a table or a portal comes from ruined-portal and bastion chests, or from casting lava with water where you want it. See $(l:lemursaucepacket:enchanting)Enchanting$(/l).$(br)$(li)$(bold)Maps:$() Xaero's minimap and world map, without mob radar or cave maps (fair play). Waystones you've activated show on both.$(br)$(li)$(bold)Voice:$() proximity voice chat. Press $(bold)V$() for

pages.title: Weekly missions
pages.text: Brassworks Missions posts a set of Create-flavoured missions every week (ESC → Missions, or $(bold)H$()). They pay coins and quest XP.
